req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET / joins post rows with users and includes the author's username in the response. Tests must verify: (1) positive — the index page returns HTTP 200 and contains usernames for known posts; (2) negative — the response does NOT contain orphaned/missing username markers; (3) boundary — the most-recent post (id=20, author_id=1, username='Rahul') appears first with its username, and the oldest post appears last. Additional tests cover multiple distinct authors appearing, exact username strings from the seed data, and that the JOIN is not broken by a missing user.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_with_author_username_positive
preconditions: Database seeded with 20 posts and 5 users as per test data
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
Inspect response status code and body for known author usernames
expected: HTTP 200 response
Response body contains 'Rahul' (author of posts 2,3,6,8,9,10,11,12,15,18,19,20)
Response body contains 'James' (author of posts 1,4,5,16)
Response body contains 'Anjali' (author of posts 7,13,14)
Response body contains 'Ishaan' (author of post 17)
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_returns_200_with_author_username_positive():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data

test_index_returns_200_with_author_username_positive()

tests.name: test_index_most_recent_post_first_with_correct_username
preconditions: Database seeded with 20 posts ordered by created DESC
Post id=20 has created='2025-04-01 10:30:37', author_id=1 (Rahul), title='Heacon signal pulse'
actions: Send GET /
Check that 'Heacon signal pulse' appears before 'Pulse ember signal' in the response body
Check that 'Rahul' appears in the response body near the most recent post
expected: HTTP 200
Title 'Heacon signal pulse' appears before 'Pulse ember signal' (ORDER BY created DESC)
Username 'Rahul' is present in the response
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_most_recent_post_first_with_correct_username():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.data
    pos_recent = data.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    pos_older = data.find(b'Pulse ember signal')
    assert pos_recent != -1, 'Most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_older != -1, 'Older post title not found'
    assert pos_recent < pos_older, 'Most recent post must appear before older post'
    assert b'Rahul' in data

test_index_most_recent_post_first_with_correct_username()

tests.name: test_index_username_field_in_db_query_result
preconditions: Database seeded with standard test data
blog.index SQL selects username via JOIN
actions: Use app context to directly query the DB and verify username column exists in result
Also send GET / and confirm HTTP 200
expected: HTTP 200 from GET /
Direct DB query returns rows with 'username' key
First row username matches expected author
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd4, path4 = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd4)
app4 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path4})
with app4.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    rows = db.execute(
        'SELECT p.id, title, body, created, author_id, username'
        ' FROM post p JOIN user u ON p.author_id = u.id'
        ' ORDER BY created DESC'
    ).fetchall()
    assert len(rows) == 20
    first = rows[0]
    assert first['username'] is not None
    assert first['username'] == 'Rahul'
    assert first['title'] == 'Heacon signal pulse'
    assert first['author_id'] == 1
client4 = app4.test_client()

def test_index_username_field_in_db_query_result():
    r = client4.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data

test_index_username_field_in_db_query_result()
